headline: Your camera shouldn't have an inbox.
subhead: Zero screens. Just real moments you see when you get home.
primary text: You unlocked your phone to take one quick photo. Twenty minutes later, you're answering work emails and doomscrolling. You were right there, but you completely missed the moment. Retra is the modern disposable camera built to break that habit. It gives you one shutter button, an optical viewfinder, a built-in flash, and zero screens. No apps to set up, no Wi-Fi, and nothing buzzing in your hand. You point, click, and drop it back into your pocket. It holds up to 500 photos on a single charge. When you get home, plug it into your phone or laptop with USB-C and find all your photos waiting for you like a freshly developed roll of film. Keep the memory. Stay in the room.
FR headline: Prends la photo. Oublie les notifications.
notes: QA pass, try 1. Camera (Obsidian) matches reference; one hand, five fingers. Phone screen softened in compositing so its tiny UI text is unreadable.

headline: They'll remember your face, not your phone.
subhead: Capture real childhood candids without disappearing behind a screen.
primary text: Watch a kid when you pull out your phone. The laugh stops, the smile goes stiff, and they wait for you to look back up. They do not want a staged photoshoot. They just want you there with them. Retra captures the memory without stealing your attention. There is no screen to check, no apps to fiddle with, and no notifications pulling you into work. Just an optical viewfinder, a built-in flash, and a single shutter button. Snap the pancake flip or the crayon masterpiece, then set it down. It holds up to 500 photos on a charge. Tonight, plug the USB-C cable into your computer and look through the genuine smiles together. Be the parent who was actually looking.
FR headline: Ils retiendront ton regard, pas ton écran.
notes: QA pass, try 1. Camera (Blossom) matches. Composition changed from the brief's over-the-shoulder view so the camera FRONT faces the viewer (no back-of-camera reference exists). Hands correct; natural faces.

headline: Don't watch the trip through glass.
subhead: Up to 500 candid shots per charge. Zero scrolling in line.
primary text: You paid for the park tickets and the hotel. The last thing you should be doing is staring into a six-inch phone screen. Standing in line, you pull out your phone for one photo of the kids, and immediately get sucked into unread emails or social feeds. Suddenly, the whole afternoon slips past behind glass. Retra slips into your pocket and stays out of the way. There is no screen to review, no settings menu, and no Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or apps. Just point through the viewfinder, click the shutter, and get right back to the roller coaster. It packs four built-in vintage and film filters, an on-camera flash for evening fireworks, and enough battery for 500 shots. When you get back to the hotel, plug it into your phone with USB-C and relive the day together. Live the day first. See the shots second.
FR headline: Aucun écran entre toi et la magie.
notes: QA pass on try 2. Try 1 rejected: street read as a Disney park (Victorian main street, castle-like spire, mouse-ear balloons). Try 2 is a generic fair midway; two stall signs with garbled lettering softened in compositing. Camera (Sol) hangs tilted on a strap and matches the reference.

headline: See Europe. Not your feed.
subhead: 500 shots per charge. Relive the trip once you get home.
primary text: You did not fly across the Atlantic to spend your golden hour checking whether your vacation photo looks good enough. The problem with phone cameras is the review loop. You take a photo, look at the screen, retake it three times, and then spend ten minutes picking a filter while the sun drops behind the rooftops. Retra brings back genuine travel candids. You look through the viewfinder, click the shutter button, and keep walking down the alleyway. No screen to critique. No social apps pinging. Just you and the city. With up to 500 photos per charge and four built-in film filters, it handles entire days of exploring. Once you are back at your room, plug the USB-C cord into your phone to unload the memories. Spend your trip looking at the sights, not at glass.
FR headline: Vis l'Europe. Pas ton fil d'actualité.
notes: QA pass on try 2. Try 1 rejected: the two women had the same face (AI tell). Camera (Chalk) matches; hands correct. Camera faces the viewer instead of the friend (no back reference).

headline: Phones away. Real cameras on tables.
subhead: Skip the developing fees and capture every unposed guest moment.
primary text: Single-use wedding cameras mean costly photo lab fees, forgotten film rolls, and guests who end up scrolling their phones. You want your reception to feel like a party, not a room full of people staring down at illuminated screens. Retra is the modern reusable alternative for guest tables. Place one beside each centerpiece. Guests pick it up, look through the real viewfinder, snap with the built-in flash, and put it right back down. There is no tiny screen to huddle around, so the dance floor stays full. Each camera holds up to 500 photos per charge with zero film rolls to buy or mail off to a lab. The next morning, export every shot straight to your laptop over USB-C. Real table candids from your favourite people, without the lab bill.
FR headline: Téléphones rangés. Appareils sur la table.
notes: QA pass, try 1. Chalk + Obsidian cameras match. Place-card line typeset in the landing-page hand font (Shantell Sans) onto the blank card.

headline: Watch the show with your own eyes.
subhead: Point, click, and put it away. Feel the music instead.
primary text: You paid serious money for tickets just to stare at a glowing wall of other people's phones recording the encore. Nobody ever watches those shaky, blown-out concert videos again anyway. Meanwhile, the band is right in front of you and everyone is busy checking their camera angles. Retra lets you capture the night without turning into a camera operator. When you are out, point through the viewfinder, pop the built-in flash for a quick crowd shot, and drop it back into your pocket. Zero screen glare. No social media notifications pulling you out of the music. Just grainy, authentic flash photos you will export over USB-C the next morning. Enjoy the set. Keep the shots.
FR headline: Regarde le show de tes propres yeux.
notes: QA pass, try 1. Camera (Chalk) matches, flash firing. Phones show no readable content; no band/artist logos. She holds the camera casually facing the viewer (no back reference).

headline: One button. No menus. Grandma approved.
subhead: No touchscreen to smudge and no account setups to remember.
primary text: Every new gadget comes with a forgotten password, a mandatory update, and a settings menu nobody asked for. If you have ever spent Christmas morning doing tech support for your parents or grandparents, you already know the dread. Retra solves that completely. It works like the classic film cameras they grew up using, but without the hassle of film rolls or photo labs. There is one shutter button, an optical viewfinder, and a built-in flash. No Wi-Fi, no Bluetooth, and no app store logins. They take up to 500 photos of the grandkids on one charge. When they want to see them, simply plug the USB-C cable into their laptop or desktop. The photos pop up right in their folder. A thoughtful holiday gift they can pick up and use in ten seconds.
FR headline: Un seul bouton. Aucun menu compliqué.
notes: QA pass, try 1. Camera (Pine) matches; both hands correct; natural wrinkles/skin. Text kept left of her face.

headline: 4 built-in film looks. Zero editing.
subhead: Four built-in styles. Now $99, compare at $165.
primary text: You do not need Lightroom or a subscription app to get that grainy, nostalgic 2000s disposable look. Retra features four built-in filters: Vintage, Black & White, Natural, and Film. No phone required, no cloud accounts, and no monthly editing subscriptions. You get candid, textured photos straight out of the camera, complete with a built-in flash and up to 500 shots per battery charge. Compare at $165 CAD, now on sale for $99 CAD (40% off). Plug into your computer or phone via USB-C to view your shots. Upgrade your daily camera roll with real point-and-shoot film vibes.
notes: QA pass, Kie render try 1 (3 earlier submits failed with Kie 'Internal Error', no image, not billed). Base scene has no product; the tiles crop out an invented camera that Kie put at the bottom edge of the scene. The four looks are the landing page's filter settings applied to one render: ILLUSTRATIVE, replace with real Retra sample photos before launch. Product shown is the real Pine cutout. subhead: One for you, two for gifts. 500 photos per charge.
primary text: Holiday shopping for friends and family just got much easier: buy two Retra cameras, and we will add a third one for free. Retra is a reusable digital camera built like a modern disposable. It combines the candid charm of classic photography with convenient USB-C export. No ongoing film expenses, no app downloads, and no Wi-Fi. Choose your favorite mix across all five body colours: Chalk, Obsidian, Blossom, Sol, and Pine. Each unit comes with a built-in flash, four film filters, and up to 500 photos per charge. Keep one in your own bag for weekend trips, and wrap the other two for the people who need a break from their phone screens. Stock is limited for this batch. Build your bundle before colours run low.
